title: I made a playable SRPG using vibe coding
author: mint_ai_songs
selftext:
This is my first time trying vibe coding to build a mobile-playable web SRPG.

From character concepts and core mechanics, to content planning, writing requirement docs, playtesting, creating a teaser trailer, and building a landing page — the whole process took me about one month.

My original goal was simple: to make a tactical game that I’d personally want to pick up and play on my phone during free time. Because of that, this project is free and non-commercial.

If you’re curious, feel free to check it out — and I’d genuinely love any feedback. I’m also happy to answer questions about the dev process or tools.

🌿 Game site ▶ [https://garden.mintfantasia.com/](https://garden.mintfantasia.com/)

🎬 Character teaser ▶ [https://youtu.be/XS0E5czwxOU](https://youtu.be/XS0E5czwxOU)

comments.author: ELPascalito
comments.body: This look lovely! Especially the characters, does it scale well on desktop screens?

replies.author: mint_ai_songs
replies.body:
Thanks! 😊  
Yes — the characters are pixel art by design.

I work with relatively large source assets and do some light post-processing, mainly so the game downscales on desktop instead of being upscaled.

Combined with a fixed aspect ratio layout, this helps keep the characters looking consistent on larger screens.

comments.author: AvailableProcess2059
comments.body: Looks incredible! What engine are you on? And how did you do the graphics, they are stunning.

replies.author: mint_ai_songs
replies.body:
Thanks a lot! Generating the art and music has been my favorite part of the whole process😊  

Engine-wise, it’s a web-based setup built using Google AI Studio.

For the graphics workflow:

\- I define a visual direction first (character proportions, color palettes, outfits, overall style).

\- Character art is generated with Gemini Pro based on those constraints.

\- I then do light post-processing in Photoshop to refine details and maintain consistency.
